sumInsured: As per Policy Schedule (not provided in extract)

great.name: Restore Benefit (Unlimited; same & different illness) — 'Unlimited Automatic Recharge'
great.quote: “Unlimited Automatic Recharge... re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year... Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness as well as different Illnesses.”
great.explanation: This is a strong restore feature: after you fully use the base Sum Insured in a policy year, the insurer can restore it unlimited times, and it works even for the same illness.

great.name: Built-in Additional SI buffer after exhaustion (acts like extra SI) — Unlimited Automatic Recharge
great.quote: “The Company agrees to automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year... utilized only after the base Sum Insured has been completely exhausted”
great.explanation: This creates additional available coverage after the base sum insured is exhausted (buffer/extra SI during the same policy year).

great.name: NCB / Renewal Bonus (Non-resetting on claims) — Cumulative Bonus
great.quote: “At the end of each Policy Year, the Company will enhance the Sum Insured by 10% flat... (vi) In the event of a Claim there is no impact on the accrual of Cumulative Bonus.”
great.explanation: Bonus continues to accrue even if you make a claim, which is better than standard NCB that often reduces/resets after a claim.

great.name: ICU Charges: No limit
great.quote: “The eligible ICU Charges applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is 'No limit'”
great.explanation: No separate cap on ICU room charges during hospitalization (still subject to overall Sum Insured).

good.name: Room Rent (default): Single Private AC Room
good.quote: “The eligible Room Rent or Room Category applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is 'Single Private AC room'.”
good.explanation: Single Private AC room is industry-standard. Higher room category can lead to proportionate deductions (pro-rating) on associated medical expenses.

good.name: PED waiting period: 36 months
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage...”
good.explanation: PED waiting period is 3 years, which is within the acceptable/standard range.

good.name: Specific Illness / Named Ailment waiting period: 24 months
good.quote: “Named Ailment Waiting Period... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...”
good.explanation: 2-year named ailment waiting is standard in many policies.

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days
good.quote: “30-day waiting period... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident...”
good.explanation: 30 days is standard. Accidents are typically covered from day 1.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization cover: 60 days
good.quote: “For a period of 60 days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission to the Hospital...”
good.explanation: 60 days pre-hospitalization is standard/good (note: paid via reimbursement only as per wording).

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover: 90 days
good.quote: “For a period of 90 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge from the hospital...”
good.explanation: 90 days post-hospitalization is standard/good (note: paid via reimbursement only as per wording).

bad.name: Consumables / Non-medical items not covered (out-of-pocket)
bad.quote: “Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – I to Policy Terms & Conditions).”
bad.reference: Clause 4.2 (1) Specific Exclusions + Annexure I (List of Expenses Generally Excluded)
bad.explanation: Consumables/non-medical items (e.g., gloves, masks, kits, etc., as per Annexure I) are excluded, meaning you may pay these from your pocket during hospitalization.
